generator_view.scenario: I want to buy one phone now and still use it happily and safely in 2031. It also contains three dated personal reports: an iPhone 6s kept since 2016 with several aging symptoms, a five-year iPhone 7 with an unresolved microphone problem after battery service, and an eight-year iPhone 6 that still functioned while several apps stopped supporting iOS 12.5. General background covers screen burn-in, service life, repairability, modular smartphones, and planned obsolescence. The packet has no verified current-unit condition report, no current support-end promise for a 2026 candidate, no controlled phone-to-phone longevity study, and no population failure rates.
